_doc: Translator glossary. `brands` are never translated or transliterated — messages carry them as {{@id}} tokens (see I18N_GLOSSARY in core/i18n.js). Each language section maps an English UI term to the one word used everywhere in that language. Add a section per language pass (L10 hi → L24 zh). `terms` defines each product term once (meaning, how to translate it, banned renderings) — see STYLE.md.

terms._doc: One meaning per English term, for the source (STYLE.md) and every translator. "translate" = how to carry the concept; "banned" = renderings that change the meaning and fail review. Brands are in `brands` (never translated); each language section holds the chosen word.

chips.def: Virtual game chips used for stakes in Dangal games (Poker, Teen Patti, Rummy, Live 1v1). Earned and lost only inside the app.
chips.translate: The word for gaming/casino chips or tokens. Make clear they are play chips, not money.
chips.note: Chips can never be bought, cashed out or converted. Party games use points, never chips.

points.def: Score inside one game or party round. Not carried between games.
points.translate: The ordinary word for points / score.

Party Hub.def: Dangal’s party night screen: one host runs a set of party games (Charades, Imposter, Most Likely To…) for a group.
Party Hub.translate: A short descriptive name ("party hub", "party corner"); may stay "Party Hub" in Latin-script languages.

Pass & Play.def: Party mode on ONE phone passed around the room; no sign-in or internet needed.
Pass & Play.translate: Describe passing a single phone around ("pass the phone"). Keep it short — it is a mode chip.

Room mode.def: Party mode across several phones: everyone joins the host’s room with a code or link.
Room mode.translate: The word for a (virtual) room people join; contrast with Pass & Play.

Manch.def: Dangal’s game library (“stage”) — every game, sorted by genre. A Dangal section name.
Manch.translate: Keep the name “Manch” (transliterate in non-Latin scripts). If a gloss is needed: “game library”.

Khel.def: Dangal’s daily games corner: Game of the Day and daily challenges. A Dangal section name.
Khel.translate: Keep the name “Khel” (transliterate in non-Latin scripts).

Khabar / Sawaal.def: The two Akhbaar modes: Khabar = today’s news cards, Sawaal = the quiz questions about them. Akhbaar mode names.
Khabar / Sawaal.translate: Keep the names (transliterate in non-Latin scripts); describe in plain words where the UI explains them.

Sabha / Mitra.def: Baithak section names: Sabha = all chats in one list; Mitra = friends and groups.
Sabha / Mitra.translate: Keep the names (transliterate in non-Latin scripts); explain in plain words where the UI explains them.

Split.def: A Baithak “instant”: a quick photo or note left for friends in the Splits tray; friends can react; it expires like a story.
Split.translate: Keep “Split” as a feature name or use the language’s word for a quick shared snap. Not a payment term.

Streak.def: Consecutive days a user (or two friends) did the daily thing — Akhbaar quiz, chat, game. Shown with 🔥.
Streak.translate: The common app word for a daily streak / run of days in a row.
banned: winning streak only (it is any daily activity)

Streak Freeze.def: An item that protects a streak for one missed day.

Teen mode.def: Settings applied automatically for users under 18 by date of birth: stricter Peepal and discovery filters, 18+ games hidden, DMs from friends only.
Teen mode.translate: Neutral, respectful: “teen mode” / “mode for under-18s”. Not childish.

Languages I read.def: The languages a user reads; feeds rank these higher and Translate uses the first one. Separate from the app language.
Languages I read.translate: First person (“Languages I read”) as a settings row; not “languages I speak”.

Region.def: The user’s country setting. Drives currency, phone code, date / time format, first day of week, units and regional content (Akhbaar sources, icebreakers, seasonal cards, Dangal defaults). Not the language.
Region.translate: The word for country / region in settings.

friend.def: A mutual relationship between two personal accounts.
friend.note: English uses “friends” for people; “connection” only means a network connection.

follower.def: Someone who follows a (usually Professional) profile without a mutual friendship.
follower.translate: The usual social-app word for follower.

post.def: Something a user publishes (Duniya, Peepal) — noun and verb.
post.translate: The usual social-app word for a post / to post.

share.def: Send something to a person, a chat or another app.

sign in.def: Use your account on this device (also: sign out, sign up; noun “sign-in”).
sign in.translate: The platform-standard verbs for sign in / sign out / sign up in the language.

Live.def: A game played in real time against another person over the internet (Live 1v1, Live tables).
Live.translate: The usual word for live / real-time play.

Practice.def: Playing against AI or solo; no rating or chips at stake.

verify.def: Confirm an email or phone with a link or a 6-digit code.
verify.translate: Standard verb for verifying an account.

hi._style: Devanagari, polite आप, warm everyday Hindi with the loanwords people actually say. Buttons: short polite imperative (सेव करें, देखें). Sentence end: । (keep ? ! …). Nuqta spellings (फ़, ज़, ख़, ग़). Western digits. Gender-neutral: prefer ergative (आपने … किया), noun or passive phrasing; when a verb must agree with आप use the honorific plural (-ते हैं), and with a third person {{name}} use ने or the honorific plural. Keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, emoji and {{tokens}} as they are.
hi.question: सवाल
hi.chess: check / checkmate / stalemate / c: शह / शह और मात / स्टेलमेट / कैसलिंग

ur._style: Urdu in Perso-Arabic script (rendered Nastaliq), RTL. Polite آپ, warm everyday Urdu — genuine Urdu vocabulary (Persian/Arabic-origin words Urdu speakers use), never Hindi transliterated into Urdu script; English loanwords where that's what people say. Buttons: polite imperative (محفوظ کریں، دیکھیں). Punctuation: ۔ full stop, ، comma, ؟ question mark (keep ! …). Western digits (0–9). Gender-neutral where possible; when a verb must agree with آپ use the plural (-تے ہیں), with a third person {{name}} use نے or the plural. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens, bidi-isolated by the runtime). Keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, emoji and {{tokens}} as they are.
ur.question: سوال
ur.chess: check / checkmate / stalemate / c: شہ / شہ مات / اسٹیل میٹ / کیسلنگ

bn._style: Standard colloquial Bengali (চলিত ভাষা) understood in Bangladesh and West Bengal. Polite আপনি, warm and everyday; English loanwords where natural (পোস্ট, চ্যাট, প্রোফাইল, লাইভ). Buttons: polite imperative (সেভ করুন, দেখুন). Sentence end: । (keep ? ! …). Write Western digits (0–9) — the runtime shows Bengali numerals for Region BD. Verbs aren't gendered; keep pronouns neutral (তিনি/উনি for third person). Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens).
bn._bd_in: Where Bangladeshi and West Bengal vocabulary differ, use the form both read comfortably: water → পানি/জল avoided where possible (use 'পানীয়' or rephrase); invite → আমন্ত্রণ জানান (not দাওয়াত / নেমন্তন্ন); greetings → হ্যালো / স্বাগতম (no religion-specific greetings); salt/egg/shop etc. standard forms (লবণ, ডিম, দোকান).
bn.question: প্রশ্ন

ta._style: Friendly modern written Tamil in Tamil script, polite நீங்கள் (plural verb endings keep it gender-neutral). Neither செந்தமிழ் coinages everyday users wouldn't recognise nor heavy English transliteration: widely used Tamil app terms where they exist (அமைப்புகள், தேடல், நண்பர்கள்), loanwords where people really say them (போஸ்ட், சாட், புரொஃபைல், லைவ்). Buttons: short imperative (சேமி, பகிர், மீண்டும் முயல்). Tamil renders long — keep UI labels concise (aim ≤ 1.6× the English length). Western digits. Understandable in India, Sri Lanka, Singapore, Malaysia. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens).
ta.question: கேள்வி

te._style: Friendly modern everyday Telugu in Telugu script, polite మీరు (plural verb endings keep it neutral). Neither grandhika/overly formal coinages nor heavy English transliteration: common Telugu app words where they exist (సెట్టింగ్‌లు, వెతకండి, స్నేహితులు), loanwords people really say (పోస్ట్, చాట్, ప్రొఫైల్, లైవ్). Buttons: short polite imperative (సేవ్ చేయండి, షేర్ చేయండి). Telugu runs long — keep UI labels concise (≤ 1.6× English). Western digits. Understandable in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens).
te.question: ప్రశ్న

mr._style: Genuine Marathi in Devanagari — never Hindi (आहे not है, नाही not नहीं, मध्ये not में, साठी not के लिए, करा not करें; scripts/lib/mr-hindi-leak.js flags these). Respectful तुम्ही, friendly modern everyday Marathi; loanwords with Marathi spelling of English sounds (ॅ/ॉ: चॅट, पोस्ट, प्रोफाइल, लाइव्ह, सेव्ह). Buttons: polite imperative -ा (सेव्ह करा, शेअर करा, पाहा). Gender: Marathi past tense is gendered — prefer present/imperative or noun phrases for anything addressed to the user; use select (female/male/other) only when the gender is known, never default to masculine. Western digits (Devanagari numerals via the Settings digit option). Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens).
mr.question: प्रश्न
mr.chess: check / checkmate / stalemate / c: शह / शह आणि मात / स्टेलमेट / कॅसलिंग

pa._style: Gurmukhi script, polite ਤੁਸੀਂ, warm everyday Punjabi as spoken in Punjab (India) and the diaspora (Canada, UK, US, Australia). Genuine Punjabi grammar and words (ਹੈ/ਹਨ, ਨਹੀਂ, ਵਿੱਚ, ਲਈ, ਅਤੇ, ਪਰ, ਤੁਹਾਡਾ, ਇਜਾਜ਼ਤ, ਵਾਰੀ), not Hindi written in Gurmukhi; no Sanskritised coinages. Loanwords people really say (ਪੋਸਟ, ਚੈਟ, ਪ੍ਰੋਫਾਈਲ, ਲਾਈਵ, ਗੇਮ, ਐਪ, ਲਿੰਕ). Buttons: short polite imperative (ਸੇਵ ਕਰੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਵੇਖੋ). Verbs are gendered: prefer imperative, present or noun phrasing; never default to masculine. Sentence end: । (keep ? ! …). Keep labels close to English length (≤ 1.4×). Western digits. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ as they are.
pa.question: ਸਵਾਲ

kn._style: Friendly modern everyday Kannada in Kannada script, polite ನೀವು (polite plural -ಿರಿ endings keep it gender-neutral; neutral phrasing for third person). Neither heavily Sanskritised/archaic coinages nor heavy English transliteration: common Kannada app words where they exist (ಸೆಟ್ಟಿಂಗ್‌ಗಳು, ಹುಡುಕಿ, ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, ಅಧಿಸೂಚನೆ), loanwords people really say (ಪೋಸ್ಟ್, ಚಾಟ್, ಪ್ರೊಫೈಲ್, ಲೈವ್, ಗೇಮ್, ಆ್ಯಪ್, ಲಿಂಕ್). Buttons: short polite imperative (ಉಳಿಸಿ, ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, ನೋಡಿ, ಮತ್ತೆ ಪ್ರಯತ್ನಿಸಿ). Kannada runs long — keep UI labels concise (≤ 1.6× English). Western digits. Understandable across Karnataka and the diaspora. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ as they are.
kn.question: ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ

ml._style: Friendly modern everyday Malayalam in Malayalam script (reformed script with chillu letters ൽ ൻ ർ ൾ ൺ, as on phones), polite നിങ്ങൾ; present and imperative forms keep it gender-neutral, keep third person neutral. Neither stiff Sanskritised coinages nor heavy English transliteration: common Malayalam app words (ക്രമീകരണം, തിരയുക, പങ്കിടുക, അറിയിപ്പ്), loanwords people really say (പോസ്റ്റ്, ചാറ്റ്, പ്രൊഫൈൽ, ലൈവ്, ഗെയിം, ആപ്പ്, ലിങ്ക്). Buttons: short polite -ുക imperative (സേവ് ചെയ്യുക, പങ്കിടുക, കാണുക). Malayalam renders among the longest — always pick the shortest natural label for buttons, tabs, chips, HUD and notification titles (≤ 1.6× English). Western digits. Understandable in Kerala, Lakshadweep and the Gulf/Western diaspora. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ as they are.
ml.question: ചോദ്യം

ar._style: Friendly, clear Modern Standard Arabic (الفصحى) for readers across the Gulf, Levant, Egypt, Iraq, the Maghreb and the diaspora — never dialect, not stiff legalese (precise MSA only on legal pages). Gender-neutral by default: buttons and instructions use the verbal noun / masdar (حفظ، مشاركة، إرسال، إعادة المحاولة), passive or impersonal forms (تم الحفظ) and noun phrases. No slash or bracket gender forms (مستخدم/ة، عزيزي/عزيزتي، (ة)) and no o/a, @, x or · markers; where direct address truly needs gender use {_g, select, female {…} male {…} other {…}} with a neutral rephrased `other` — never masculine by default; third-person {{name}} phrasing stays neutral. Common Arabic app vocabulary (الإعدادات، منشور، دردشة، الملف الشخصي، مباشر), loanwords only where Arab users really say them (فيديو، كاميرا، بريميوم). Punctuation: ، ؛ ؟ (keep . ! …); no tatweel; tashkeel only to disambiguate. Arabic letters only — never Persian/Urdu letters (ی ک ہ ے ں ٹ). ICU plurals: all six categories zero/one/two/few (3–10)/many (11–99)/other (100+) with correct noun agreement (لا أعضاء / عضو واحد / عضوان / # أعضاء / # عضوًا / # عضو); plain-text counts become plural blocks on the same variable; keep =0 branches. Write Western digits 0–9 (the app shows ٠–٩ by Region). Keep buttons short. Chips are virtual (رقائق), never money words (أموال، نقود). Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ, chess notation and card ranks (A, K, Q, J) Latin.
ar.question: سؤال
ar.chess: check / checkmate / stalemate / c: كش / كش مات / تعادل بالجمود / تبييت

es._style: Neutral international Spanish, Latin-America-leaning and natural in Spain: informal tú for the user, ustedes for plural address — never vosotros/vuestro/sois/podéis. Inclusive without o/a, @, x, e or ·: neutral constructions (Te damos la bienvenida, Personas en el grupo, Quienes juegan, tus amistades / contactos, ¿Todo listo?); where neutral phrasing is truly impossible use {_g, select, female {…a} male {…o} other {…}} with a neutral rephrased `other` — never masculine by default. Shared vocabulary, no regionalisms or words rude somewhere (no coger → tomar/elegir; no guay, mola, vale, tío, ordenador, pinche, boludo); teléfono (not celular/móvil), dispositivo, video (no accent). Buttons, tabs and chips: short infinitives (Guardar, Compartir, Reintentar), ≤ 1.5× English. Punctuation: opening ¿ and ¡ always; full accents (á é í ó ú ü ñ). Write digits only — the app formats numbers/dates by Region. ICU plurals need one/many/other (many for large round numbers: many {# de puntos}); keep =0 branches and select categories. Chips are virtual (fichas), never money. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ, chess notation and card ranks Latin.
es.follower: seguidores (en frases: personas que te siguen)
es.question: pregunta

fr._style: Neutral international French understood in France, Belgium, Switzerland, Canada/Québec and Francophone Africa: friendly tu everywhere in the UI (ton/ta/tes; imperative Choisis, Partage) — vous/votre/vos only in legal.* keys, where a neutral impersonal style is fine. Inclusive without point médian (·), slashes, (e), o/a, @ or x: epicene / neutral phrasing (Bienvenue, Les membres, Ton compte, Personne, Quelqu'un, Tes contacts, C'est parti?); where neutral phrasing is truly impossible use {_g, select, female {…e} male {…} other {…}} with a neutral rephrased `other` — never masculine by default. Widely shared vocabulary — no France-only slang or Quebec-only terms; e-mail. Buttons, tabs and chips: short infinitives (Enregistrer, Partager, Réessayer), ≤ 1.5× English. Typography: no space before ; : ! ? and none inside « » (the app inserts the right narrow no-break space per Region); « » for quotes; full accents including capitals (É, À) and ligatures (œ, æ). Write digits only — the app formats numbers/dates by Region. ICU plurals need one/many/other (one covers 0 and 1; many for large round numbers: many {# de points}); keep =0 branches and select categories. Chips are virtual (jetons), never money. Brand names stay Latin ({{@…}} tokens); keep AI, OTP, PIN, URL, GIF, DM, QR, Wi-Fi, PDF, ID, FAQ, chess notation and card ranks Latin.

fr.player: joueurs (neutre: personnes qui jouent, À toi de jouer)
fr.question: question
fr.chess: check / checkmate / stalemate / c: échec / échec et mat / pat / roque
